problem:
What is the variance of the following data set?

$$
12,\,15,\,15,\,17,\,21,\,22
$$

Do not round your answer.

${\sigma }^{2}=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=6$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (12+15+15+17+21+22) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot 102 \\  & =17.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot ({12}^{2}+{15}^{2}+{15}^{2}+{17}^{2}+{21}^{2}+{22}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (144+225+225+289+441+484) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot 1808 \\  & =\frac{1808}{6} \\  & =\frac{904}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{904}{3}-{(17)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{904}{3}-289 \\  & =\frac{904-867}{3} \\  & =\frac{37}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
